content.text: I've reviewed the fee/pricing schedule, payment terms, grant of rights, and definitions, and searched the full document for parity language.

input.quote: 2. Corio Customer Application Management Revenue: Corio to pay Commerce One [*] of all Application Management Revenue from Corio Customers for use of Commerce One Software or MarketSite.net Service Access subject to the following limitations.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation / best-pricing or price-parity obligation in either direction. Full-text searches for "most favo(u)red", "favorable/favourable", "no less favorable", "best price", "other customers", "similarly situated", "match" and related parity language returned nothing, and the commercial terms (Exhibit B Pricing at p0148–p0154, Revenue Sharing Fees at p0155–p0161, Payment Terms at sec-17, Fees at sec-4) are stated as fixed fees and revenue shares with no undertaking by Corio (our party, the licensee/customer) to extend Commerce One terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers. The Distribution License (2.4) and New Products (2.9) provisions likewise create no parity commitment — future product licensing is left to terms "as the parties may agree". The preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer) is therefore already met, so no redline is proposed. Note only that certain pricing figures in Exhibit B and in Section 2.4 are redacted ("[*]"); if any redacted term contains a pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking by Corio, this rule should be re-run against the unredacted text.
